name: slam
resume: All 33 exports of slam 0.1-56 are done. Triplet matrices and sparse arrays are a port of the R and C code. NumPy holds the index and value arrays. There is no crate.

functions.name: simple_triplet_matrix
functions.done: Build a sparse matrix from 1-based row, column, and value triplets.

check.case: Build a sparse matrix from 1-based row, column, and value triplets.

proof.r:
.libPaths(c(path.expand("~/R/library"), .libPaths()))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(slam))

one <- function() {
  m <- simple_triplet_matrix(i=c(1,2,1), j=c(1,1,2), v=c(1,2,3), nrow=2, ncol=2)
  as.numeric(as.matrix(m))
}
value <- one()
elapsed <- numeric(20)
for (i in seq_len(20)) {
  t0 <- as.numeric(Sys.time())
  one()
  elapsed[[i]] <- as.numeric(Sys.time()) - t0
}
cat(sprintf(
  "{\"value\":[%s],\"median_ms\":%.17g}\n",
  paste(sprintf("%.17g", value), collapse = ","),
  median(elapsed) * 1000
))
proof.python:
import statistics
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

from slam import *
from slam._arrays import as_array, as_matrix


def one():
    m = simple_triplet_matrix([1, 2, 1], [1, 1, 2], [1, 2, 3], 2, 2)
    return np.ravel(as_matrix(m), order='F')

value = np.ravel(np.asarray(one(), dtype=float), order="F")
elapsed = []
for _ in range(20):
    started = __import__("time").perf_counter()
    one()
    elapsed.append((__import__("time").perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
print(
    '{"value":[%s],"median_ms":%.17g}'
    % (
        ",".join("%.17g" % float(part) for part in value),
        statistics.median(elapsed),
    )
)
